defendant: William A. Boyd; Linda L. Boyd; New Jersey Property Liability Insurance Guaranty Association; Educap Inc; Remax Executive Reality Inc; and Arisdad Holdings, LLC
description:
SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY
CHANCERY DIVISION - SALEM COUNTY
DOCKET NO.
F-010325-25
SHERIFF NO.
26000149
PLAINTIFF -
Carrington Mortgage Services, LLC
DEFENDANT -
William A. Boyd; Linda L. Boyd; New Jersey Property Liability Insurance Guaranty Association; Educap Inc; Remax Executive Reality Inc; and Arisdad Holdings, LLC
By virtue of a Writ of Execution in the above stated action to me directed, I shall expose for sale at public venue at the Salem County Courthouse, situated at No. 92 Market Street, in the City of Salem, New Jersey on
Monday,
August 10, 2026
at
2 o’clock
in the afternoon, ALL the following lot, tract or parcel of land and premises, situate, lying and being in the Borough of Penns Grove, in the County of Salem and State of New Jersey, bounded and described as follows:
Any 3rd Party Buyer who bids on this sale will be purchasing both properties and one deed will be provided.
Municipality: Penns Grove
County of Salem
State of New Jersey
Street and Street No.: 15 Spring Street Penns Grove, NJ 08069
Tax Block and Lot No.: Parcel #1: Block 137 fka 1, Lot 11 (15 Spring Street)
Parcel #2: Block 96, Lot 5 (7 Spring Street)
Dimensions of Lot (approximately): 58.22 x 113.3 x 6.91 x 70.06 x 46.03 x 18.75 x 81.71 Feet (Irregular)
Nearest Cross Street: Garnet Street
The Mortgaged Premises consists of two separate lots known as 15 Spring Street, Borough of Penns Grove, NJ, which is further described as Lot 11, Block 137 (formerly Block 1) on the tax map of Borough of Penns Grove, and 7 Spring Street, Township of Carneys Point, NJ, which is further described as Lot 5, Block 96 on the tax map of Carneys Point Village, with a combined mailing address of 15 Spring Street, Penns Grove, NJ 08069.
A full legal description of the premises can be found in the offices of the County Clerk and the Sheriff of Salem County.
The approximate amount of the judgment to be satisfied by said sale is the sum of $97,303.30 together with the costs of this sale.
The approximate upset price is $105,949.48.
The upset price may be subject to further Orders of additional sums.
Occupancy Status: Unknown
Taxes- Due 5/1/2026 $1,742.72 Open
Sewer- 01/01/2026 - 03/31/2026 $152.00
Open Plus Penalty $1,828.00 Open Plus Penalty; Owed in Arrears
To the best of this firm's knowledge, the property is not an affordable unit subject to the Fair Housing Act.
Terms of Sale: 20% of bid in cash, certified check or cashiers check from the successful bidder upon conclusion of sale. The Sheriff’s Office cash limit is $1,000.00 The balance is due within 30 days of the date of sale.
Surplus Money:
If after the sale and satisfaction of the mortgage debt, including costs and expenses, there remains any surplus money, the money will be deposited into the Superior Court Trust Fund and any person claiming the surplus, or any part thereof, may file a motion pursuant to the Court Rules 4:64-3 and 4:57-2 stating the nature and extent of that person’s claim and asking for an order directing payment of the surplus money. The Sheriff or other person conducting the sale will have information regarding the surplus, if any.
The Sheriff reserves the right to adjourn the sale without further notice through publication.
McCalla Raymer Leibert Pierce, LLC
, Attorneys for Plaintiff
Charles M. Miller, Sheriff
